t: Pagan Lithuanian dukes, united after their victory at Saule in 1236, built one of the largest states of medieval Europe.
Ruled by the Gediminid dynasty, it absorbed much of Rus' and used Ruthenian as its chancery language.
Joined to Poland from 1386 and in the Commonwealth from 1569, it was partitioned, mostly to Russia, by 1795.
dyk: Lithuania was the last pagan state in Europe: its official conversion to Catholicism began only in 1387, and that of Samogitia not until 1413.
ev: Lithuanians destroy the Livonian Brothers of the Sword at the Battle of Saule
Mindaugas is crowned king of Lithuania
Gediminas invites Western settlers in letters naming Vilnius as his seat
Algirdas defeats the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters
Jogaila begins the conversion of Lithuania to Catholicism
Vytautas and the Poles defeat the Teutonic Order at the Battle of Grunwald
The Union of Lublin creates the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
The Third Partition gives almost all remaining lands to the Russian Empire

f.capital: Vilnius (from the early 14th century); earlier seats included Kernavė and Trakai
